house.description: C.J. Ramstad/North Shore State Trail Master Plan update to allow for all-terrain vehicle use on a portion of the trail funding provided, and money appropriated.

House.text: Introduction and first reading, referred to Environment and Natural Resources Finance and Policy
Committee report, to adopt and re-refer to Ways and Means

bill_text.text_with_changes:
A bill for an act relating to natural resources; appropriating money to update the C.J. Ramstad/North Shore State Trail Master Plan to allow for all-terrain vehicle use on a portion of the trail.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1. [+APPROPRIATION; C.J. RAMSTAD/NORTH SHORE STATE TRAIL MASTER PLAN UPDATE. +]

[+$25,000 in fiscal year 2026 is appropriated from the all-terrain vehicle account in the natural resources fund to the commissioner of natural resources to update the C.J. Ramstad/North Shore State Trail Master Plan to allow for all-terrain vehicle use on those portions of the trail that lie within Cook and Lake Counties. By February 1, 2026, the commissioner must report to the chairs and ranking minority members of the legislative committees with primary jurisdiction over environment policy and finance on the modifications made to the master plan under this section. +]
bill_text.plain_text:
A bill for an act relating to natural resources; appropriating money to update the C.J. Ramstad/North Shore State Trail Master Plan to allow for all-terrain vehicle use on a portion of the trail.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1. APPROPRIATION; C.J. RAMSTAD/NORTH SHORE STATE TRAIL MASTER PLAN UPDATE.

$25,000 in fiscal year 2026 is appropriated from the all-terrain vehicle account in the natural resources fund to the commissioner of natural resources to update the C.J. Ramstad/North Shore State Trail Master Plan to allow for all-terrain vehicle use on those portions of the trail that lie within Cook and Lake Counties. By February 1, 2026, the commissioner must report to the chairs and ranking minority members of the legislative committees with primary jurisdiction over environment policy and finance on the modifications made to the master plan under this section.
